test_policy.notes: DBU calls itself 'test-preferred': ACT, SAT or CLT scores are not required for admission, and applicants without scores get a holistic review, but scores are strongly encouraged and are used for merit scholarships. The international checklist does not state a different rule.

requirements.notes: Apply on DBU's own online application; the undergraduate checklist states 'Application fee: $0'. The international checklist asks for transcripts, a passport copy, an essay ('Why I Want to Study at DBU', 250 words minimum), English test scores (not required for students entering the Intensive English Program) and, for an I-20, financial documents. A minimum GPA for international freshmen was not found. Admission is rolling and no application deadline is published; DBU only says some financial aid has priority deadlines (no dates printed), so the deadline list is empty. The Fall 2027 IEP term starts Aug. 10, 2027.

english_policy.waiver_notes: No proof of English needed for citizens of, or those who earned a high school diploma or one full year of university study in, listed English-speaking countries (e.g. Australia, Bahamas, Canada except Quebec, Ghana, Jamaica, New Zealand, South Africa, Trinidad and Tobago, United Kingdom). Other options: SAT EBRW 500+, IB Higher-Level English A1 score of 5, AP English Language 3, KCSE English grade B. English scores are good for 2 years. DBU has an English Language Institute with an Intensive English Program (five 8-week sessions a year); applicants entering the IEP do not need English test scores, but the terms for moving from IEP to degree study were not found.

english.notes: The PDF (updated March 2026) lists 'TOEFL 4' for undergraduates without naming the scale; the value fits the 1-6 scale. An old 0-120 minimum is not published. The same sheet also lists MET 65 and iTEP 3.7 for undergraduates.
IELTS Academic overall band 6.0 with no section band below 5.0.
Duolingo English Test 100 with no subscore below 90.

aid.notes: The larger international awards are restricted: International Academic Scholarships ($8,000-$14,000 a year, tuition only, by GPA/test/class rank, up to eight semesters) and the Christian Service Scholarship ($4,000 a year, plus up to $3,000 Christian Leadership) are open to students from Canada, Mexico, or affiliated with ACSI schools or DBU Global Community partner schools, and require on-campus housing. The International Student Scholarship, open to any new international student on need and merit, is generally a one-time grant of $500 to $2,500. International students are not eligible for federal aid. Percentages of aid recipients are not published for international students.
